submission.natural_language_explanation: This is a retrospective token-identity dial rather than a content detector: strength is -GELU(z) of the layer-2 pre-activation, so it is capped at GELU's global minimum (0.170) and the scan's top examples all tie exactly at that ceiling without sharing a meaning. Peak strength is set by the current token: it sits at or near the ceiling (0.14-0.17) on prenominal quantifiers/determiners (a, one, some, any, each, both, many, most, all, several, few, another) and possessive determiners (my, your, our, his), is exactly 0.000 on demonstrative/relative pro-forms (it, its, this, that, these, those, which, such, whose), standalone possessives (mine, yours, hers, ours) and third-person object pronouns (him, her, them) - where the positive pole fires instead - and is weak (<=0.09) on articles, prepositions, copulas and content words (the, to, by, on, was, is, and, file, back); personal pronouns (he, she, they, who, me, us, you) are context-dependent and land between 0.04 and 0.17, and because 'a', 'is', 'of', 'and', 'in' and 'have' still clear 0.25x scale, only text built entirely from the weak class is predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Sets ' that' as an object demonstrative against prior art claiming 'that' is the meaning: the hypothesis places demonstratives at exactly 0.000 (the positive pole fires there), so with only weak-class fillers it predicts no activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: On the back shelf the folder was this, and the rest was on the desk.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests ' this' as a bare pronoun before a comma rather than a determiner, with no claimed quantifier anywhere; the hypothesis keeps demonstratives at exactly 0.000, so it predicts inactivity despite the topic words around them.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The dealer traded such back to the owner of the file.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses ' such', named in the hypothesis's exactly-0.000 pro-form class, with no head noun after it, and the remaining tokens (the, back, to, of, file) are weak class, so the peak is predicted at zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The porter put these on the back of the file and left.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests ' these' used as a bare pronoun in an unusual object position; the hypothesis gives demonstratives exactly 0.000 and the sentence contains no claimed activating determiner, so it predicts no activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The technician filed its maintenance report on the back desk.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests ' its', which the hypothesis places in the demonstrative/possessive pro-form class at exactly 0.000, inside a technical sentence whose other tokens are weak class (the, on, filed, report, desk).

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The dealer sold the depot whose contract was on the back of the file.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Uses ' whose' as a relative determiner, predicted exactly 0.000 by the hypothesis's pro-form class, while a competing reading would call it a possessor; the other tokens are weak class so no ceiling token can rescue the peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The file on the back shelf was mine, and the rest was on the desk.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Standalone possessive ' mine' as a predicate complement is explicitly 0.000 in the hypothesis even though it is possessive in meaning; the trigger sits mid-sentence so it is measured, and every other token is weak class.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The detective found those on the back shelf of the store room.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Tests ' those' as a demonstrative determiner, predicted exactly 0.000 by the hypothesis and predicted to fire the positive pole rather than this negative one, with only weak-class words otherwise.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The instructor split them into two groups before the test.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Third-person object pronoun ' them' is explicitly 0.000 in the hypothesis while prenominal determiners sit at the ceiling; every other token here is weak class (the, into, before, test), so the peak should be zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The courier brought him the envelope at the desk by the door.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Third-person object ' him' as an indirect object is in the hypothesis's exactly-0.000 class; the sentence puts it mid-clause so it is measured, and no claimed quantifier or possessive determiner appears.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The clerk gave the parcel to her before the meeting.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Third-person object ' her' after a preposition is in the hypothesis's exactly-0.000 class, in a sentence whose other tokens (the, to, before, parcel, meeting) are weak class, so the predicted peak is zero.
